intro.h2: A Greater Madison design-build firm that starts by listening
paragraphs: Degnan Design-Build-Remodel has offered kitchen remodeling in Madison, WI and the towns around it since Bob Degnan founded the company in 1981. His son Abe grew up on job sites as a helper and carpenter, then earned an architecture degree and brought a design-first approach to the family business.

Today the same team designs, prices and builds each project. A designer draws several concepts, then 3D drawings, before anyone swings a hammer. A lead carpenter runs the site once work starts. In GuildQuality surveys, 95% of clients say they would recommend the firm and 98% call the team professional and organized.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Madison, WI, and the rest of the house

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: From open-concept kitchens for entertaining to efficient updates and kitchen additions. Recent projects include a kitchen with laundry in Lodi, a dual-island kitchen in DeForest and a 1970s kitchen reworked for a retired couple. Most kitchen builds take about 2 to 3 months.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel in DeForest, WI with wood cabinets, white subway tile, quartz counters and a corner sink under three windows

items.name: Master Suite and Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites, steam showers, soaking tubs, powder rooms and tub-to-shower conversions. The team has remodeled baths in Wexford Village, Maple Bluff, Waunakee and East Madison. Plan on about 1.5 to 2.5 months of construction for a bathroom.

image.alt: Ensuite bathroom remodel in DeForest, WI with dual wood vanities, backlit mirrors and a green linen tower

items.name: Aging-in-Place Remodeling
items.blurb: Abe Degnan holds the CAPS designation for aging-in-place work. The portfolio shows curbless showers, grab bars and open kitchens planned for later years, including an affordable aging-in-place bath in Brooklyn, WI and a contemporary one in Maple Bluff.

image.alt: Aging-in-place bathroom remodel in Maple Bluff, WI with a brass grab bar, white cabinetry and open display shelving

items.name: Finished Basements
items.blurb: Degnan calls it a finished lower level, because it should look and feel like the rest of the house. Past projects include media rooms, a wet bar, an exercise room and a lower-level living room in Oregon, WI. Basement builds usually run about 2 to 3 months.

image.alt: Finished lower-level living room in Oregon, WI with blue board-and-batten wainscoting, a wood staircase and framed family photos

items.name: Condominium Remodeling
items.blurb: Condo work means HOA approval, building rules and shared walls. Degnan has remodeled units in Metropolitan Place, Weston Place, Hawks Reserve, Nolen Shores and The Marina Condominiums, plus a transitional condo kitchen and mudroom in Middleton.

image.alt: Condominium kitchen remodel in Middleton, WI with cherry cabinets, stainless appliances and a round dining table

why_choose_us.h2: What sets the Degnan team apart

items.title: Two generations, one family name
items.text: Bob Degnan started the company in 1981. His son Abe now leads it as president and Director of Design, and Zach Degnan works on the design team.

items.title: Scores you can check
items.text: Independent GuildQuality surveys show 95% of clients likely to recommend Degnan, 96% satisfied with communication and 98% who felt the team was professional and organized.

items.title: Award-winning work
items.text: Wins include Wisconsin Builders Association Builder of the Year in 2024 and NARI Madison Contractor of the Year for a residential kitchen under $100K in 2023.

items.title: They come back after the job
items.text: You get lien paperwork, product manuals and warranties at the end. The team also checks in at 6 months and 1 year to catch any warranty work.

about.h2: Meet Abe Degnan, president and Director of Design
about.text: Abe Degnan learned the trade as a helper and carpenter in his father's company. After earning an architecture degree from UW-Milwaukee, he brought a design-first approach to the firm Bob Degnan founded in 1981. Abe now leads the team as president and Director of Design, mentors the designers and runs day-to-day operations. He holds the CGR, CGB and CAPS designations. His stated goal for every job is that it finishes on time, on budget and more beautiful than you imagined. Abe is also a proud father of six.

image.alt: Abe Degnan, president of Degnan Design-Build-Remodel

process.h2: Nine steps, three phases: how a Degnan project runs

steps.title: A first conversation
steps.text: A free call about your project, your goals and a ballpark budget. Photos of your space help the team give you a useful range.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: After a consultation and budgeting meeting, a designer measures, sketches several concepts and develops the best one into 3D drawings.

steps.title: Selections and estimating
steps.text: Your designer goes with you to showrooms. Trade partners walk your home so the estimate is accurate and change orders stay rare.

steps.title: Contract and preparation
steps.text: You sign a contract with agreed start and finish dates. Degnan pulls permits, places orders and hands the job to your lead carpenter.

steps.title: Build and follow-through
steps.text: The crew protects your home and controls dust. After a final walk-through, the team checks in at 6 months and 1 year.

service_area.h2: Remodeling across Madison and Dane County
service_area.text: Degnan works from its office on Lake Road in Windsor and builds throughout Greater Madison. That includes Madison neighborhoods such as Middleton Hills, Nakoma, Maple Bluff, Shorewood Hills and the University area, plus the Dane County towns below and the Lake Wisconsin area. The team also has experience in luxury and high-rise condominiums such as Metropolitan Place and Weston Place.

items.a: Yes. Ballpark budget talks are free and happen by phone, video chat or at the Windsor office. You share your wish list, photos and budget goals. If you want a full design, written budget and scope of work, that starts with a paid design retainer.

items.q: How long does a kitchen or bathroom remodel take?
items.a: Design, selections and estimating usually take a few months. After that, Degnan's typical build times are 2 to 3 months for a kitchen, 1.5 to 2.5 months for a bathroom and 2 to 3 months for a finished basement. The firm says 90% of its projects fall in these ranges.

items.q: Can we live at home during the remodel?
items.a: Most Degnan clients do. Before work begins, the crew protects your home and sets up dust control. Payments follow the progress of the work, and you meet with your lead carpenter, designer and production manager from time to time so you always know what is happening next.

items.q: Are the photos on the website really Degnan projects?
items.a: Yes. Degnan states that it does not use stock photos and that every project shown is its own work. Its reviews are real too: client surveys are published on GuildQuality, and more project and in-progress photos are posted on its Facebook and Houzz pages.

items.q: Can you help before we buy a house?
items.a: Yes. Send the MLS listing and photos, and the team will spend about half an hour with you by phone or video at no charge to talk through whether the home can be remodeled the way you want. Realtors can use the same service for clients.

final_cta.h2: Start with a free ballpark budget call
final_cta.text: Tell the Degnan team about your kitchen or bath, and get a realistic range before you commit to design.
